title: Counting table with a threshold and a hashed bucket
summary: A table counts how often each bucket has been seen; buckets come from hashing the symbol, and the readout returns the most counted bucket once its count passes a threshold.
core_idea: Count hashed symbol buckets in a table and read the bucket whose count passes a threshold.

state.name: quorrel
state.meaning: Table of counts, one per bucket, incremented whenever a symbol lands in that bucket.

readout.name: read
readout.latex: y_t = lookup(quorrel) if count >= theta, sum over buckets
readout.plain: y_t = lookup(quorrel) if count >= theta, sum over buckets

learning.description: The threshold theta is set by hand; nothing is trained.
learning.few_shot_argument: Fixture only: no claim about learning speed is made beyond the toy case.

complexity.constants_notes: A handful of operations per symbol in the toy setting.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Fixture only: the rule is fixed by hand.

prediction.statement: A bucket seen twice is read after two symbols.

capabilities.prediction: Reports the most frequent bucket once it is seen twice.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: Counting tables are a standard data structure.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: Fixture only; no difference is claimed.

falsifiers: The reported bucket is not the most counted one.

toy_example.description: Counts five symbols into four buckets.
